newsitem.title: sri lanka: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Separatist Tamil rebels kill 22 soldiers in an attack on a army rout-clearing operation in eastern Trincomalee district.
About 300,000 of the 500,000 or so civilians, who fled northern Jaffna peninsula during security forces offensives to capture it in 1995 and 1996, have now returned, officials say.
Some 15,000 nurses in government hospitals to go on one-day token strike on Monday to protest against non-implementation of proposed salary rivisions.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) leader Velupillai Prabhakaran now hiding in the jungles of Iranamadu near Mullaitivu in northeastern Sri Lanka, military officials say.
Ruling People's Alliance invites minority Tamil political parties to join its May Day meeting.
Government postpones all university educational activities and examinations due to an on-going strike by some university staff trade unions.

One person killed as police open fire on some 500 protestors who clashed with police during a demonstration against the proposed construction of Sri Lanka's only coal power plant in the island's northwest.
All universities close as strike by university staff trade unions continues.
